sourceEvidence.label: Vanguard Trust Lab public distribution candidate

assessment.summary: Private authoring and public research software require an enforced distribution boundary; the clean-history split-public design is selected.

nonNegotiables: No restricted identity or private deliverable in public files, Git objects, assets, or releases.
Public claims use publicly accessible primary evidence.
assumptions: No measured CI latency or memory budget was supplied.
Public lineage does not need to preserve private development history.

opportunities.title: Separate private authoring from public research software
opportunities.summary: Create an allowlisted public snapshot with a clean Git history and fail-closed publication gate.
opportunities.diagnosis: Privacy enforcement would drift if it remained distributed across manually copied source, metadata, assets, workflows, and releases.

evidence.claim: The private authoring boundary contains material that must not enter public history.
The public candidate began without inherited Git metadata.
One mandatory verifier can reduce public-policy drift across file classes.
Git, Pages, workflow artifacts, images, and releases are separate public surfaces.

desiredInvariants: Every public file is deliberately selected or produced by an approved transform.
No public Git object shares ancestry or storage with the private repository.
Public claims depend only on publicly retrievable sources.
Unknown or prohibited classifications block publication.

options.title: Rewrite and scrub existing history
options.summary: Rewrite blobs, authors, refs, tags, and releases, then add a publication gate.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Known canonical objects can be rewritten, but external copies may remain.
This option does not use the available clean-history boundary.
A rewrite does not prevent recurrence without the publication gate.
Every release and public surface must also be purged.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known canonical objects can be removed, but uncontrolled copies and omissions remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect every rewritten ref, object, identity, release, and archive.

tradeoffs.assessment: The deployed static Lab is unchanged; rewrite cost is offline.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare browser behavior before and after publication.

tradeoffs.assessment: Runtime memory is unchanged; rewriting needs temporary object and pack storage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record rewrite peak RSS and temporary disk use.

tradeoffs.assessment: Force-pushes invalidate commit IDs, tags, pull requests, and clones.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run the rewrite in a mirror and exercise clone recovery.

tradeoffs.assessment: Refs, caches, releases, and collaborators require coordinated migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory each controlled surface and rehearse the runbook.

tradeoffs.assessment: History rewriting is complex and difficult to reverse after exposure.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Preserve a private mirror and verify a complete mapping before swap.

residualRisks: Previously copied objects and assets cannot be recalled.
A missed ref, cache, log, or release can retain restricted data.
Recurrence remains possible without a mandatory publication gate.

acceptanceCriteria: All canonical objects and public assets pass the public-data policy
migrationNotes: Coordinate invalidated commit IDs and clones
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore the protected private mirror before the rewritten repository is published.

options.title: Clean-history split-public
options.summary: Select and validate a public snapshot, then initialize a new Git object database.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Private objects are never imported; the selected files still require sanitization.
The design directly uses the clean-history opportunity.
The verifier owns the fail-closed publication policy.
Pages and release workflows reuse the same validation, while manual host actions still need review.

tradeoffs.assessment: The public object database cannot inherit private blobs, refs, authors, tags, or releases.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect all public objects, refs, identities, remotes, Pages files, and archives.

tradeoffs.assessment: The static runtime is unchanged; scanning adds only build-time work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare Lab behavior and record publication-gate wall time.

tradeoffs.assessment: The Lab is unchanged; verification reads a small bounded source tree.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record verifier peak RSS if repository size grows materially.

tradeoffs.assessment: False positives block publication without affecting the deployed static Lab.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise negative fixtures and the release failure path.

tradeoffs.assessment: Two boundaries and deliberate patch porting require recurring discipline.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Trial source, UI, image, and release updates through the documented flow.

tradeoffs.assessment: One clean initialization avoids destructive ref coordination.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rebuild the public repository using only the sanitized snapshot and instructions.

residualRisks: Public hosting and contributor identities remain visible by platform design.
Manual releases or host-setting changes can bypass source controls.
Scanner false negatives and third-party caches remain possible.

migrationNotes: Do not merge or graft private history later
implementationReadiness.rollback: Before publication, discard and regenerate; after publication, treat escaped data as copied and issue a corrected release.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the clean-history split-public design because private lineage has no required public compatibility value.

openQuestions: When should hosting move to a project organization?
What CI cost should trigger scanner optimization?
When would custom response headers justify moving from GitHub Pages?
